title: Electric Circuits
seo_title: Grade 4 Electric Circuits Worksheets: Open and Closed Circuits, Conductors and Insulators
standard_text: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on electric circuits (NGSS 4-PS3-2): batteries, bulbs, switches, open and closed circuits, conductors and insulators, with circuit pictures. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Current only flows around a complete, closed circuit.
key_sub: A battery pushes current through wires to a bulb and back. A gap, an open switch or an insulator stops it.
body_html:
How to think about it

An electric circuit is a complete loop. Current flows from the battery, through wires and a bulb (or buzzer or motor), and back to the battery. The current carries energy.

A closed circuit has no gaps, so the bulb lights. An open circuit has a gap (an open switch, a loose wire or an insulator), so nothing works.

Conductors (metals, graphite) let current flow. Insulators (plastic, rubber, wood, glass) do not.

Example

A plastic straw is placed across a gap in a circuit. Does the bulb light?

Plastic is an insulator.

The circuit stays open.

Answer: No.

Example

A bulb is attached to a battery with one wire. Does it light?

Current needs a path out and back.

Answer: No, the loop is not complete.

Common mistakes

  • Using one wire. A circuit needs a complete loop.
  • Thinking any object closes a gap. Only conductors do.
  • Thinking the switch makes electricity. It only opens or closes the path.

faq.q: What is the difference between an open and a closed circuit?
faq.a: A closed circuit is a complete loop, so current flows and the bulb lights. An open circuit has a gap, so no current flows.
Conductors, like metals and graphite, let electric current flow. Insulators, like plastic, rubber, wood and glass, do not.

faq.q: Why does a bulb need two connections?
faq.a: Current must flow out of the battery, through the bulb and back to the battery. One wire does not make a loop.

items.q: What does a switch do?
c: It opens or closes the circuit.
items.e: Closing the switch completes the path; opening it makes a gap.

items.q: Why are wires coated with plastic?
c: Plastic is an insulator that keeps the current inside the wire.
items.e: The metal inside conducts; the plastic outside protects us.
